findings.description: The checkout-copy scanner only recognizes literal `git checkout`, so `git -C . checkout spike/example src/file` bypasses SP-1. The other checkout matcher requires `--`, which this valid path-copy command omits.
findings.failure_mode: Git copies prototype content into the working branch despite the explicit prohibition on copying from spike branches.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same Git global-option parsing for both checkout checks, and add coverage for path copies using `-C` and `-c` without `--`.

findings.description: The research scope check compares porcelain status entries rather than file contents. Overwriting an already modified file outside research leaves the same status entry and passes. Restoring a dirty file also passes because `comm -13` ignores removed entries.
findings.failure_mode: Research can overwrite or discard existing repository edits while the scope check reports success.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot file contents or hashes before dispatch and compare afterward, including files already dirty or untracked. Check both additions and removals, and restrict allowed changes to the single assigned report.

findings.description: A detached worktree shares repository refs with the main checkout, but the probe checks only working-tree status. A probe such as `git update-ref -d refs/heads/topic` deletes the real topic branch without changing that status.
findings.failure_mode: The helper exits successfully after a probe deletes or rewrites repository refs; removing the throwaway worktree does not restore them.
findings.suggested_fix: Run probes in an independent repository with isolated refs and configuration rather than a linked worktree.

findings.description: SP-1 documents (header lines 824-826) that `git checkout <spike ref> <path>` (path copy without `--`) is blocked. The no-`--` form is enforced only by `_sp1_checkout_copies`, whose segment extractor is `grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+checkout[[:space:]]+[^;&|]*'` on `$_cmd_match`. That requires `checkout` to follow `git` immediately. The three regex rules in the same block deliberately accept `git -C <dir>`, `git -c k=v` and `git --opt[=v]` prefixes via `$_sp1_git`, but the copies helper does not. `git -C . checkout spike/x path/to/file` (or `git --no-pager checkout spike/x file`) matches no segment, so the helper returns 1; the `--` regex needs a literal `--`, so nothing fires and the spike content lands in the working tree of the current branch. `git -C` is a common agent idiom, not an exotic evasion. Secondary: `yes | git checkout -p spike/x` copies every hunk of the spike into the worktree with one operand (n=1), so it also passes, yet it is not in the documented misses list.
findings.failure_mode: The documented SP-1 block for path copies is bypassed by any `git <global-opt> checkout spike/<slug> <path>` command; spike content enters a non-spike branch, violating D-5.4 while the hook claims to enforce it, and the fence corpus (which only has bare `git checkout`) stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same prefix in the segment grep: `grep -oE 'git([[:space:]]+(-C|-c)[[:space:]]+[^[:space:];&|]+|[[:space:]]+--[a-z-]+(=[^[:space:];&|]+)?)*[[:space:]]+checkout[[:space:]]+[^;&|]*'` (the existing `${seg#*checkout}` strip still works). Treat `-p|--patch` with a spike first operand as a copy (block when n>=1 and a patch flag is present). Add `git -C . checkout spike/x file` and `yes | git checkout -p spike/x` to tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl.

findings.description: Confirms and extends the primary reviewer's concern 1. The predicate's result is the exit status of `yq ... 2>/dev/null | jq -e ...`. Without pipefail that is jq's status alone. On jq 1.6 (still the default on Debian/Ubuntu LTS and macOS system installs) `jq -e` with empty stdin exits 0 (the `exit 4 when no output` behaviour arrived in jq 1.7). So any yq failure (unparsable ledger, yq permission error, yq killed) turns into `return 0`, `_fr11_all_merged` hits `continue`, and `git branch -D spike/<slug>` is allowed even though the branch is unmerged and undecided. The header comment promises 'any failed lookup keeps the block'; this path does the opposite. Note this is not caught by the version gate on line 650, which checks yq only.
findings.failure_mode: A safety hook fails open: with a corrupt or unreadable decisions.yaml, `git branch -D spike/<slug>` deletes an unmerged, undecided spike branch. The PR's own test 'an unparsable ledger keeps the block' fails on hosts with jq 1.6.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture first and check: `local json; json=$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null) || return 1; [[ -n "$json" ]] || return 1; printf '%s' "$json" | jq -e ... >/dev/null 2>&1`. Alternatively wrap the pipeline in `( set -o pipefail; ... )`. Also require the jq result to be literally `true` by capturing stdout rather than relying on `-e` semantics across jq versions.

findings.description: Confirms and extends the primary reviewer's concern 5 with evidence from inside this diff. The new map-epic guard parses `br show --json` as `if type == "array" then .[0] else . end`. The same PR's chart-ticket.sh `first_obj` (line 110) and chart-frontier.sh FILTER both additionally handle the `{"issues": [...]}` envelope, so the author knows br can emit that shape. In the envelope case the object has no `.labels`, the jq succeeds and prints `no`, the `unknown` branch is not taken, and a sprint task is created under the map epic. D-4.7 says this must be refused before any br call. The guard fails open on exactly the shape the rest of the PR defends against.
findings.failure_mode: With a br release that wraps `br show --json` in an `issues` envelope, a build-type bead is created as a child of a /chart map epic; the map's frontier then contains a non-question child and sprint planning sees a task parented to a planning-only epic.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse one parser: `(if type == "array" then (.[0] // {}) elif type == "object" and has("issues") then (.issues[0] // {}) else . end)`. Additionally fail closed when no issue object is found (empty array / empty issues): treat 'no labels field at all on a non-empty object' as `unknown` rather than `no`.

findings.description: The build-path filter drops beads only when `.issue_type == "question"`. chart-frontier.sh in the same PR reads the type as `.issue_type // .type // ""`, and the header of get-ready-work.sh promises 'they are dropped from the ready set whatever labels they carry'. If a br release reports the field as `type`, every question bead passes through untouched and `/implement` and `/run` will claim decision tickets as work. The failure is silent because the fallback is 'keep'.
findings.failure_mode: Decision tickets appear in `/implement` and `/run` work selection; an autonomous run could claim and 'implement' a question bead.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same accessor as chart-frontier.sh: `select(((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question")`, and add a test case in the br stub that emits `type` instead of `issue_type`.

findings.description: `op_close` rejects rows, closes beads and the epic, appends `## Closed` and sets the map Status, but never removes or archives the hand-off snapshot `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` written by `op_handoff` (line 393). The snapshot's first line is '# Priority-1 context: these decisions are settled; confirm, do not re-ask'. plan-and-analyze.md loads `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` at priority 1 (line 44) and, separately, `grimoires/loa/context/*.md` at priority 2 (line 50), a superset glob. Phase 0 prose says 'Other snapshots are not ingested', but the frontmatter will load every snapshot, including closed ones, at priority 2 on every future `/plan-and-analyze`. With two maps ever handed off, the stale snapshot also stays a candidate for `golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots` unless that function re-reads each map doc's Status (not visible in the truncated golden-path.sh hunks); the unattended rule then exits 1 with 'more than one open map'.
findings.failure_mode: After a map is consumed, its 'settled, do not re-ask' decisions keep being injected into unrelated later cycles' PRD interviews; a second handed-off map can make unattended `/plan-and-analyze` refuse to start.
findings.suggested_fix: In `op_close` (both --consumed-by and --reason paths) move the snapshot to `grimoires/loa/context/archive/chart-<slug>-<date>.md` or delete it (it is fully reproducible from the map doc and ledger). In plan-and-analyze.md exclude `chart-*.md` from the priority-2 glob (or document that the P1 entry supersedes it) so the frontmatter matches the Phase 0 prose. Have `golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots` ignore snapshots whose map doc Status is `closed`/`abandoned`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The verdict depends on what the main session's hooks write under .run/ and .beads/ during the Agent call; the primary reviewer reports PostToolUse hooks append to .run/audit.jsonl on every tool call, which I cannot refute from the diff.
findings.description: `research-end` fails the ticket if any file under `.run/` or `.beads/` is newer than the dispatch marker. The subagent (chart-researcher.md) has only Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch/Write, so it cannot touch those directories; anything newer there was written by the parent session's own tooling (hooks firing on the Agent call and on the subagent's Write, beads sqlite side files, run-state heartbeats). The check therefore measures the host, not the subagent, and will produce false FAIL verdicts whenever any hook logs to .run/. Because the `newer` branch exits 1 before the report is even checked, a correct report is discarded and the ticket stays open.
findings.failure_mode: Every research dispatch on a host with audit/telemetry hooks writing to .run/ fails with 'the research subagent changed files outside grimoires/loa/research/' even though the subagent wrote only its report.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the mtime scan of .run/ and .beads/ (the subagent has no Bash and no br), or restrict it to paths the subagent could plausibly write and exclude known hook sinks (.run/audit*.jsonl, .run/*.log, .beads/*.db-wal/-shm). Prefer a positive check: hash the tracked tree (`git diff --stat`, `git ls-files -o --exclude-standard`) plus `.beads/issues.jsonl` before/after instead of mtimes.

findings.description: The throwaway worktree shares the main repository's `.git` (object store, refs, config, hooks, remotes). The only post-condition is `git status --porcelain` of the main tree, which cannot see: `git update-ref`/`git tag`/`git branch -f` on refs not checked out, `git push` to a remote, edits to `.git/config` (e.g. `core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, aliases, credential helpers) or to `.git/hooks/*`, all of which the probe argv can perform with its inherited credentials. The header claims the helper 'exits 1 when the main tree's status changed' as the ticket's write fence; these mutations persist after `worktree remove` and execute on the operator's next commit.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe (agent-authored argv) can alter refs, push, or plant a hook/config entry in the shared .git while the helper reports 'main tree unchanged' and exits 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot and compare `git for-each-ref`, `sha256sum .git/config .git/hooks/*` and `git remote -v` before/after alongside `git status`; run the probe with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and an empty credential helper, and consider `git clone --shared --no-hardlinks` into the scratch dir instead of a linked worktree so ref writes land in the throwaway clone.

findings.description: The scope check is `comm -13` over porcelain status lines before/after. A tracked file that was already modified (` M path`) at research-begin produces the identical line after further edits, so a subagent Write to any already-dirty tracked file is invisible, as is a Write that overwrites an already-untracked file. The same status-string equality is used by chart-unblock-probe.sh line 72. Both are documented as the write fence for the respective ticket types.
findings.failure_mode: On a dirty working tree (the normal state mid-session) a research subagent can modify any already-modified App-Zone file without the ticket failing.
findings.suggested_fix: Record content identity, not status: `git diff --no-ext-diff | sha256sum` plus `git ls-files -o --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 sha256sum` before/after, or `find "$ROOT" -newer "$m" -type f -not -path '*/.git/*' -not -path '*/grimoires/loa/research/*'` which already exists in the script for .run/.beads.

findings.description: Idempotency and consistency gaps. (a) `rule-out` on a bead whose row is already `decided` (operator-confirmed via /decisions) skips the ledger reject (only open/proposed are rejected), yet still closes the bead with 'out of scope' and appends an 'Out of scope' bullet, while the same row remains cited under 'Decisions so far'. The map doc then lists the decision both as settled and as ruled out, and the handoff snapshot propagates that to the PRD. `op_resolve` by contrast refuses rejected/superseded rows explicitly. (b) `op_resolve` re-run after `br close` failed (line 317) finds `rst=proposed`, `bst!=closed`, and runs `br comments add` again (line 316) before retrying close, leaving duplicate 'Proposed:' comments. (c) `map_rows` scans pending files under `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/` rather than `$ROOT`, so with `--root` the live tree's worktree ledgers are merged into a fixture map.
findings.failure_mode: A decided row can be marked out of scope on the bead and map doc while the ledger says decided; partial-failure re-runs of resolve leave duplicate bead comments.
findings.suggested_fix: In `op_rule_out` die when `rst` is `decided` (or `rejected`/`superseded`) with 'open a new ticket'. In `op_resolve` check for an existing 'Proposed: ... (ROW)' comment (br comments list) or add the comment only when `rst` was `open` on entry. Use `${G}/a2a/` in `map_rows`.

findings.description: The FR-1.1 exception grants `git branch -D spike/<slug>` on the strength of a row in the tracked file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml having `status: decided` and a transition `by: operator:*`. That file is plain YAML the agent can rewrite with the Write/Edit tools (the Bash hook does not see those), so the agent can self-author the operator transition and then delete an unmerged spike branch. dec-write-lib.sh presumably only emits `operator:*` on confirm, but nothing here verifies the row came through it (no signature, no git-history check that the transition commit was not authored in the current session).
findings.failure_mode: A compromised or prompt-injected session edits decisions.yaml, then deletes an unmerged spike branch that was the only pointer for a pending decision; the hook reports it as allowed.
findings.suggested_fix: Require that the decided row is present in the committed ledger (`git show HEAD:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) rather than the working copy, or that the spike branch is pushed (`git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` equals the local head) so deletion cannot lose the pointer; document the residual trust in the header.
